name: AWS Access Key ID
description: An AWS Access Key ID was found in source. Paired with a Secret Access Key, this gives an attacker programmatic access to the linked AWS account.
remediation: Rotate the key in IAM immediately. Remove it from history with `git filter-repo` or BFG, then store credentials in environment variables or a managed secrets store (AWS Secrets Manager, SSM Parameter Store).

name: AWS Secret Access Key
description: An AWS Secret Access Key appears to be assigned in configuration or source. The pattern matches a 40-character base64-like value associated with a key named `aws_secret_access_key`.
remediation: Rotate the key in IAM, scrub the repo history, and move credentials to a managed secrets store. Set IAM policies to deny long-lived keys where possible (use STS).

name: GitHub Personal Access Token (classic)
description: A classic GitHub Personal Access Token grants the bearer the scopes assigned to the token (potentially full repo + org admin).
remediation: Revoke at https://github.com/settings/tokens. Rotate to a fine-grained PAT or a GitHub App installation token with least privilege.

name: GitHub fine-grained Personal Access Token
description: A fine-grained GitHub Personal Access Token has been exposed.
remediation: Revoke the token immediately. Use GitHub App installation tokens for production automation.

name: GitHub OAuth access token
description: A GitHub OAuth access token has been exposed.
remediation: Revoke the token via the linked OAuth app. Re-authorize the app with a new token stored server-side.

name: GitHub App installation/user token
description: A GitHub App user-to-server or server-to-server installation token has been exposed.
remediation: Revoke and rotate the installation. App tokens should be created at request time, scoped, and never persisted.

name: GitLab Personal Access Token
description: A GitLab Personal Access Token was found. Depending on its scopes it can read or write any project the user has access to.
remediation: Revoke at GitLab > User Settings > Access Tokens. Replace with a project or group token with least-privilege scopes.

name: Slack bot token
description: A Slack bot token grants the bearer the OAuth scopes installed for the bot.
remediation: Revoke at https://api.slack.com/apps and rotate. Store tokens in a secrets manager; never embed in source.

name: Slack user token
description: A Slack user OAuth token acts on behalf of the authorizing user.
remediation: Revoke the app's installation. Prefer bot tokens for automation and short-lived user tokens via OAuth flow.

name: Slack incoming webhook URL
description: Slack incoming webhook URLs let anyone who has the URL post messages into a specific channel.
remediation: Rotate the webhook in Slack. Treat webhook URLs as secrets; store them in env or a secrets manager.

name: Stripe secret key
description: Stripe secret keys allow full API access to the connected account, including refunds and payouts.
remediation: Roll the key at https://dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys. Only ever use restricted keys server-side.

name: Stripe restricted key
description: Stripe restricted keys carry a subset of permissions but still allow whatever operations were granted at creation.
remediation: Roll the restricted key. Review the linked permission set in the Stripe dashboard.

name: Twilio Account SID
description: A Twilio Account SID was found. Combined with an Auth Token it grants API access; on its own it is identifying information.
remediation: If paired with an Auth Token in source, rotate the Auth Token in the Twilio console.

name: SendGrid API key
description: A SendGrid API key grants the bearer permission to send email via the linked account.
remediation: Revoke at https://app.sendgrid.com/settings/api_keys. Replace with a scoped key, stored in env.

name: Mailgun API key
description: A Mailgun API key was found.
remediation: Rotate the key at Mailgun > API Keys. Move secrets to environment variables or a secrets manager.

name: Discord bot token
description: A Discord bot token grants full bot control for the linked application.
remediation: Regenerate the token in the Discord Developer Portal. Treat the token as a secret.

name: Discord webhook URL
description: Discord webhook URLs allow anyone who has the URL to post messages to the linked channel.
remediation: Delete and recreate the webhook in Discord server integrations. Store new URLs in a secrets manager.

name: npm access token
description: An npm access token allows publishing or installing private packages on behalf of the owner.
remediation: Revoke at https://www.npmjs.com/settings/<user>/tokens. Use granular tokens scoped to specific packages.

name: PyPI API token
description: A PyPI API token allows uploading packages.
remediation: Revoke at https://pypi.org/manage/account/token/. Use project-scoped tokens.

name: OpenAI API key
description: An OpenAI API key permits paid API calls on behalf of the project.
remediation: Rotate at https://platform.openai.com/api-keys. Store the new key in a secrets manager.

name: Anthropic API key
description: An Anthropic API key permits paid API calls.
remediation: Rotate at https://console.anthropic.com/settings/keys.

name: Google API key
description: A Google API key was found. Depending on restrictions and assigned APIs, this can incur cost or give access to data.
remediation: Restrict the key by API and referrer/IP in Google Cloud Console. Rotate if exposed.

name: Google Cloud service account key (JSON)
description: A GCP service account key file (or fragment) appears in source. Service account keys can authenticate as the service account directly.
remediation: Delete and re-create the key in IAM. Prefer Workload Identity Federation over long-lived JSON keys.

name: Private key (PEM)
description: A PEM-encoded private key block is present in source. Private keys must never live in a repository.
remediation: Treat the key as compromised: revoke or re-issue all certificates and tokens signed by it. Rotate to a managed KMS for production keys.

name: JSON Web Token
description: A JWT was found in source. JWTs often carry session or authorization claims that are sensitive.
remediation: Verify the token has actually expired and is not still accepted. Treat any JWT with active claims as a credential to rotate.

name: Password assignment in source/config
description: A password-like field is being assigned a literal string. Even placeholder credentials in config get committed to history and end up in CI logs.
remediation: Load credentials from environment variables or a secrets manager. Use placeholders like `${DB_PASSWORD}` (not a literal) in templated configs.

name: Database connection string with embedded credentials
description: A database URL with an embedded username and password was found.
remediation: Move credentials out of the URL: use IAM auth, a secrets manager, or environment variables for the password portion. Never log full DSNs.

name: Heroku API key (UUID format)
description: A Heroku API key (UUID-shaped) was found assigned to a Heroku-named field.
remediation: Rotate at https://dashboard.heroku.com/account. Use OAuth tokens or scoped CI tokens instead.
